subject: latent mediator with continuous observed indicators and a binary outcome

messages.author: b9d50b6aa7309090
messages.subject: latent mediator with continuous observed indicators and a binary outcome
parts:
Hi Yves et al.,

I have used lavaan to perform causal effects based mediation analysis for a single as well as multiple continuous mediators and a single binary outcome (and binary treatment/exposure). Thank you to Yves for sending me slides some time ago which pointed me to the paper by Muthen (2011) which then lead me to Muthen and Asparouhov (2014). Causal effects mediation modeling in SEM requires to write code beyond the SEM analysis (which provides the SEM parameter estimates) to compute the causal effects as "defined parameters" in the lavaan model specification. First it requires deriving the expectation of the outcome Y with exposure at value t and the mediator M at exposure t*, or E{Y(t,M(t*))}. For binary Y, this requires integrating the probability of Y conditional on M with respect to the distribution of M under t*. Muthen (2011) provides the mathematical details for this which helped me implement it in lavaan.

However, I now think that my data would be better fit by a continuous LATENT mediator with multiple observed (continuous) indicators. Muthen (2011) and Muthen and Asparouhov (2014) discuss latent mediators and their analysis in MPLUS, but do not provide any mathematical details/derivations about how E{Y(t,M(t*))} would now be derived or approximated (M is now the latent mediator). Now the models for outcome Y and the observed indicators all contain the latent mediator M, so it is not clear to me how to obtain E{Y(t,M(t*))}.
There are several papers (in particular Albert et al. 2016 Causal mediation analysis with a latent mediator) but they also do not seem to provide details on how to obtain E{Y(t,M(t*))} for binary Y and latent continuous M.

To summarize, I know how to do naive mediation analysis in lavaan with a binary outcome and continuous latent mediator with continuous observed indicators, but I am trying to figure out how to do the causal effects mediation analysis correctly.

Can someone help?
Thanks, Ina


Ina Hoeschele, Ph.D.
